question: Which of the following sentences uses the word "board" with a different meaning from the others?

options.text: The board of directors met yesterday.
The captain had to board the ship.
He nailed a picture of the board of directors on the wall.
The board of directors decided to hire a new CEO.

solution:
The correct answer is** option 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **To answer this question, let's first understand the meaning of the word "board" in the contexts provided:**
 
• **Board (Noun):** A group of people who manage or direct a company or organization (e.g., a "board of directors"). It can also refer to a flat piece of wood or material. (निदेशक मंडल, परिषद)
 
• **Board (Verb):** To get on or into a ship, aircraft, train, or bus. (सवार होना, चढ़ना)
 
• **Now, let's examine the given sentences:**
 
• **Option 1:** The **board** of directors met yesterday.
 
 
• This sentence uses "**board**" as a **noun** to refer to an administrative body.
 
 
 
• **Option 2:** The captain had to **board** the ship.
 
 
• This sentence uses "**board**" as a **verb**, meaning the action of entering the vessel. This is a **different part of speech and meaning** compared to the other options.
 
 
 
• **Option 3:** He nailed a picture of the **board** of directors on the wall.
 
 
• This sentence uses "**board**" as a **noun**, again referring to the group of people.
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** The **board** of directors decided to hire a new CEO.
 
 
• This sentence also uses "**board**" as a **noun** to refer to the governing body of the organization.
 
 
 
• So, **Option 2** is the only sentence that uses "**board**" with a different meaning and grammatical function.__

Therefore, the correct answer is** "Option 2."**
